statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, the following holds. Let D(x) be the largest decimal digit of the positive integer x. Call a pair of indices (i, j) admissible when 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and D(nums[i]) = D(nums[j]). If no admissible pair exists, then r = -1. If at least one admissible pair exists, then r = max{ nums[i] + nums[j] | (i, j) is admissible }, where the maximum is over all admissible pairs and addition is ordinary integer addition.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, the call max_sum(nums) returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, there exist indices i and j such that 0 <= i < j < len(nums), D(nums[i]) = D(nums[j]), and r = nums[i] + nums[j], where D(x) is the largest decimal digit of x.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, for every pair of indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and D(nums[i]) = D(nums[j]), we have nums[i] + nums[j] <= r. Here D(x) is the largest decimal digit of x.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, we have r = -1 if and only if there do not exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and D(nums[i]) = D(nums[j]), where D(x) is the largest decimal digit of x.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, either r = -1 or 2 <= r. In other words, no non-sentinel answer is 0, 1, or negative.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, either r = -1 or r <= 20000.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, r <= 2 * M, where M is the maximum value among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1].
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, if D(nums[0]) = D(nums[1]) then r = nums[0] + nums[1], and otherwise r = -1, where D(x) is the largest decimal digit of x.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with len(nums) = 2, and for every i with 0 <= i < 2, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, r = max{ nums[i] + nums[j] | 0 <= i < j < len(nums) }, where the maximum is over all index pairs.
preconditions: Let D(x) be the largest decimal digit of the positive integer x. nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000, and D(nums[i]) = D(nums[0]) for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r and max_sum(nums') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit signed integers satisfying the base constraints: each has length between 2 and 100 inclusive, and every element of each is between 1 and 10000 inclusive. Also len(nums') = len(nums), and there exists a bijection pi on {0, ..., len(nums)-1} such that nums'[i] = nums[pi(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r and max_sum(nums') returns a result r', we have r' >= r.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit signed integers satisfying the base constraints: each has length between 2 and 100 inclusive, and every element of each is between 1 and 10000 inclusive. Also nums' contains nums as a sub-multiset: there is an injective map f from {0, ..., len(nums)-1} to {0, ..., len(nums')-1} such that nums'[f(i)] = nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, if there exists at least one admissible pair, then r != -1 and for every admissible pair (i, j), nums[i] + nums[j] <= r. Here an admissible pair means indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and D(nums[i]) = D(nums[j]), where D(x) is the largest decimal digit of x.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, if p and q are the unique indices with 0 <= p < q < len(nums) and D(nums[p]) = D(nums[q]), then r = nums[p] + nums[q].
preconditions: Let D(x) be the largest decimal digit of the positive integer x. nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000, and there is exactly one pair of indices (p, q) with 0 <= p < q < len(nums) and D(nums[p]) = D(nums[q]).

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, whenever max_sum(nums) returns a result r, r = 2 * M, where M is the maximum value among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1].
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000, and the maximum value M among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1] occurs at least twice among the indices.
